claims.claim: A non-domiciled resident is taxed on foreign dividends, interest and gains only when they are remitted to Ireland

sources.name: PwC: Ireland, income determination
sources.says: Last reviewed 05 August 2026. Individuals who are resident but not domiciled are "liable to Irish income tax on foreign investment income to the extent that it is remitted into Ireland"; a non-domiciled resident is taxed on gains on Irish assets in full and on foreign gains to the extent they are "remitted to Ireland". The CGT rate is given as 33% (40% for certain fund interests and life policies); the page predates the 7 October 2026 change.

sources.name: PwC: Ireland, taxes on personal income
sources.says: Last reviewed 05 August 2026. 2026 income tax: 20% up to EUR 44,000 for a single person (EUR 53,000 / 88,000 for couples) and 40% on the balance. A resident, non-domiciled individual is taxed on Irish-source income, and other foreign income only "to the extent that it is remitted into Ireland."

sources.name: Revenue: what is domicile and the domicile levy
sources.says: Published 24 November 2025. "Everyone has a 'domicile of origin' at birth (usually the domicile of the father)." "You keep your domicile of origin unless you choose to gain a new domicile", which needs clear evidence that you intend to live permanently in the new country and do not intend to return. "Your domicile affects how foreign-source income is taxed in Ireland"; a non-domiciled resident pays tax on foreign income to the extent that it is remitted into Ireland. A remittance is funds sent to Ireland from abroad by wire, mail or online transfer. The page says nothing about loans.

claims.note: The remittance basis still exists. Not in the profile and not settled here: Ireland taxes Irish and "equivalent" offshore funds under a separate exit-tax regime (KPMG's Finance Bill 2026 page, read 2026-11-15 at https://kpmg.com/ie/en/insights/tax/finance-bill-2026/investment-funds-life-assurance.html, gives 38% falling to 35% from 1 January 2027, with the eight-year deemed disposal still a chargeable event). No page read says how US-domiciled ETFs are classed or whether the remittance basis shelters them, so nothing was added to the fact; a search result, not a read, had two retail sites disagreeing on CGT versus income tax for US ETFs. Revenue's old domicile URL (https://www.revenue.ie/en/jobs-and-pensions/tax-residence/tax-residence-and-domicile/domicile.aspx) returned 404; the current page is cited.

claims.claim: A non-domiciled parent counts as resident for CAT only after 5 consecutive years in Ireland, after which the worldwide estate is in reach

sources.name: Revenue Notes for Guidance, CAT Consolidation Act 2003, section 11 (copy on Chartered Accountants Ireland TaxSource)
sources.says: "The entire property comprised in the inheritance is liable to tax where" the disponer is "resident or ordinarily resident in the State at the date of the disposition", or the successor is at the date of the inheritance; property located in the State is liable irrespective of residence. A foreign-domiciled person is not considered resident or ordinarily resident until 1 December 2004, and then only if he or she "has been resident in the State for the 5 consecutive tax years preceding the relevant date."

sources.name: Revenue Notes for Guidance, CAT Consolidation Act 2003, section 6 (copy on Chartered Accountants Ireland TaxSource)
sources.says: The same rule for gifts: taxable "where the disponer is resident or ordinarily resident in the State at the date of the disposition" or the beneficiary is at the date of the gift; a non-domiciled person counts "only if he/she has been resident in the State for the 5 consecutive tax years preceding that date."

sources.name: Revenue: acquiring a foreign property
sources.says: Published 16 December 2025. If you receive a gift or inheritance of foreign property you "may have to pay Irish Capital Acquisitions Tax (CAT)"; "This will be the case if you, or the person that you receive the property from, are resident" or "ordinarily resident, in Ireland." The page does not mention the non-domiciled rule.

sources.name: PwC: Ireland, other taxes
sources.says: Last reviewed 05 August 2026. "There are currently no net wealth/worth taxes on individuals in Ireland." A gift or inheritance "will be subject to CAT if either the donor or the beneficiary is resident or ordinarily resident in Ireland"; assets situated in Ireland are also subject to CAT regardless of residence. The page gives no CAT rate, threshold or five-year rule. Self-employed PRSI is 4.2%, rising by 0.1% from 1 October 2026.

claims.note: Revenue's own copy of the notes (https://www.revenue.ie/en/tax-professionals/documents/notes-for-guidance/cat/2025/part02.pdf, dated 7 January 2026) came back as unreadable PDF binary, so the same Revenue notes were read as HTML on Chartered Accountants Ireland's TaxSource. The test is "the 5 consecutive tax years preceding" the year of the death, with residence or ordinary residence at that date; the profile's "5 consecutive years" and the summary's "once the parent has lived there 5 years" match. A resident beneficiary also brings the inheritance into charge, which the profile does not need (US-resident heirs). Revenue's guessed territorial page (https://www.revenue.ie/en/gains-gifts-and-inheritance/cat-territorial-rule/index.aspx) is a 404.

Employment and business are not permitted without specific permission, and holders are not entitled to State benefits or publicly funded services.
